question: Could the people who invented the alphabet read Egyptian hieroglyphs?
answer: Probably not, argues the Egyptologist Orly Goldwasser. The earliest alphabetic texts were cut by Semitic-speaking workers at Egyptian turquoise mines in Sinai, early in the second millennium BC, though dates are disputed. They took hieroglyph pictures for the first sound of each word in their own language, so an ox head, alp, wrote a.
move: A tool used by outsiders can be simpler than any expert would design.
reference: Goldwasser, How the Alphabet Was Born from Hieroglyphs, Biblical Archaeology Review 36(2), 2010
